The condition $\pi(\pi(i)) = i$ for all $i$ means $\pi$ is an involution: every cycle has length 1 or 2. The condition $\pi(i) \neq i$ removes the fixed points, so every cycle has length exactly 2.

Such a permutation is the same as a perfect matching of $\{1, \ldots, 10\}$: each 2-cycle $(a\ b)$ pairs $a$ with $b$, and each element belongs to exactly one pair.

The number of perfect matchings of $2n$ elements is $(2n-1)!! = (2n-1)(2n-3)\cdots 3\cdot 1$. For $2n = 10$:

$$9!! = 9 \cdot 7 \cdot 5 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 945.$$

As a check, choose the partner of element 1 in 9 ways. The remaining 8 elements then have $7!!$ matchings, and $9 \cdot 7!! = 9!!$.

ANSWER: 945
